summary: This is the improved version of the thermostat's display method: instead of printing the status to the console, it returns the status message as a String so the caller can decide what to do with it.

lines.text: The comment stands in for the parts of the class that do not change — the fields, the constructor, and getStatus() are all still there, and only the display method is being reworked.

The return type changes from void to String, which is the whole point of the exercise: a method that hands back a value can be checked with a single assertion, with no need to capture and restore System.out.

The method still builds the same human-readable line by calling the existing getStatus(), but now it hands that text to whoever asked for it, so the same message can go to a device display, a log, or a test.
